title: KVM private MSR namespace remains implemented with hypervisor CPUID hidden
command: powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\build.ps1; $thumb=(Get-Content raw\test-certificate-thumbprint.txt).Trim(); Set-AuthenticodeSignature bin\kprobe.sys (Get-Item Cert:\LocalMachine\My\$thumb) -HashAlgorithm SHA256; sc.exe start KProbePass; Get-Content raw\kernel-probe.txt. Setup actually used: bcdedit /set '{current}' testsigning on; sc.exe create KProbePass type= kernel start= demand binPath= "C:\adversary\work\gpt-6.1-sol-kernel-20261019-1233\bin\kprobe.sys"; shutdown.exe /r /t 5 /f.
bare_metal: A normal physical AMD Ryzen CPU does not implement the KVM paravirtual MSR interface. Linux UAPI explicitly assigns 0x4b564d00..05 to KVM wall clock/system time/APF/steal/PV-EOI/poll-control. Here five return 0 and poll-control returns 1, while unrelated invalid MSRs fault. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/arch/x86/include/uapi/asm/kvm_para.h and https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/virt/kvm/x86/msr.html . AMD APM Vol.3 RDMSR requires #GP for reserved/unimplemented addresses, but no separate CPU specification contradiction is asserted because an exhaustive model-specific reserved-address map was not established.
severity: High detection value: compact deterministic read-only probe. RDMSR requires CPL0; ordinary user APIs cannot perform this measurement. On this guest an administrator/SYSTEM needed a signed kernel driver, testsigning and a reboot; physical arbitrary kernel software cannot implement a real extra MSR without instruction interception/emulation or tampering with this probe.
repro: From the assigned pass directory, follow repro-load.ps1: build with build.ps1, create/import local test certificate, sign driver, enable testsigning and reboot if needed.
Create demand-start kernel service KProbePass pointing to the absolute bin\kprobe.sys path. Run sc.exe start KProbePass. DriverEntry performs all probes automatically.
Read raw\kernel-probe.txt and confirm CPL=0 and KPROBE COMPLETE; sc.exe query KProbePass must report RUNNING. Stop before each repeat so DriverEntry runs again.
Source uses this pass absolute output path; update it if reproducing in another directory.
controls_and_limitations: Two successful loads on different observed APIC IDs reproduced the namespace response. All MSR probes read only; no WRMSR.
RDMSR 0x480, 0x40000000..03, 0xDEADBEEF and 0xFFFFFFFF produce C0000096, ruling out a blanket zero-return policy and validating SEH.
CPUID.1 ECX bit31 is clear and selected 0x40000000 leaves return zero; their absence is not evidence against virtualization.
No claim that this identifies the exact host build or excludes another hypervisor emulating KVM interfaces. VBS/HVCI were off before any lab changes.
This is an explicit indexed interface identifier, not a speculative reserved-MSR contradiction.
privilege_and_driver: kernel; NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM started demand-start WDM driver KProbePass (bin\kprobe.sys, SHA256 BCD462F7A3A53B52D6A819B46FA88F11D7FD2915710591749D88D307CA515589); DriverEntry CS=0010 CPL=0 IRQL=0. Driver compiled with LLVM/MinGW, test-signed; test-signing boot required.

bare_metal: QEMU documents a firmware-configuration selector at x86 I/O port 0x510 and byte data at 0x511, a big-endian count and 64-byte directory records. The measured protocol returns 17 coherent records including genroms/kvmvapic.bin and opt/ovmf/X-PciMmio64Mb. These identify a KVM virtual APIC option ROM and OVMF virtual-machine firmware configuration, rather than a standard AMD physical desktop interface. Source: https://www.qemu.org/docs/master/specs/fw_cfg.html ; implementation: https://github.com/qemu/qemu/blob/master/hw/i386/fw_cfg.c .
severity: High detection value: a small kernel driver can reproduce the bounded selector/data read; no DMA, memory scanning or host access is needed. IN/OUT are privileged in ordinary Windows applications. This pass required a test-signed driver and a testsigning reboot.
repro: From the assigned pass directory, follow repro-load.ps1: build with build.ps1, create/import local test certificate, sign driver, enable testsigning and reboot if needed.
Create demand-start kernel service KProbePass pointing to the absolute bin\kprobe.sys path. Run sc.exe start KProbePass. DriverEntry performs all probes automatically.
Read raw\kernel-probe.txt and confirm CPL=0 and KPROBE COMPLETE; sc.exe query KProbePass must report RUNNING. Stop before each repeat so DriverEntry runs again.
Source uses this pass absolute output path; update it if reproducing in another directory.
controls_and_limitations: Driver writes read-only selectors 0,1,0x19 to port 0x510; it never writes data or DMA. Directory count limited to less than 256, names bounded to 56 bytes.

Signature read twice returns AMIF, not QEMU. DMA signature is AMIF CFG. Identification relies on the coherent protocol and explicit KVM/OVMF directory strings, not a false claim of receiving QEMU magic.
Read directory metadata only; did not access option-ROM payload, firmware logs, UUIDs or externally supplied file contents.
A custom physical FPGA/firmware device could deliberately imitate this interface; the independent KVM MSR evidence corroborates actual virtualization.
The probe changes the device read cursor/selector; no firmware configuration blob was modified.

title: Kernel PCI configuration reports QEMU Standard VGA identifier
command: powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\build.ps1; $thumb=(Get-Content raw\test-certificate-thumbprint.txt).Trim(); Set-AuthenticodeSignature bin\kprobe.sys (Get-Item Cert:\LocalMachine\My\$thumb) -HashAlgorithm SHA256; sc.exe start KProbePass; Get-Content raw\kernel-probe.txt. Setup actually used: bcdedit /set '{current}' testsigning on; sc.exe create KProbePass type= kernel start= demand binPath= "C:\adversary\work\gpt-6.1-sol-kernel-20261019-1233\bin\kprobe.sys"; shutdown.exe /r /t 5 /f.
evidence:
KPROBE version=3 DriverEntry=FFFFF8062EAF1000 CS=0010 CPL=0 IRQL=0 CR0=0000000080050033 CR3=00000000001AE000 CR4=0000000000B50EF8
PCI 00:01.0 vendor=1234 device=1111 revision=02 class=030000 subsystem=0000:0000 header=00
KPROBE COMPLETE
bare_metal: QEMU Standard VGA specification assigns PCI ID 1234:1111 to its PCI display adapter; revision 2 is documented for QEMU extended registers. A standard physical desktop GPU is not this QEMU virtual adapter. Source: https://www.qemu.org/docs/master/specs/standard-vga.html .
severity: Easy to detect; this measurement used a kernel driver and HalGetBusDataByOffset, but the same PCI ID is ordinarily available in PnP user-mode enumeration without a custom driver. PCI identifiers can be spoofed or emulated, so corroboration matters.
repro: From the assigned pass directory, follow repro-load.ps1: build with build.ps1, create/import local test certificate, sign driver, enable testsigning and reboot if needed.
Create demand-start kernel service KProbePass pointing to the absolute bin\kprobe.sys path. Run sc.exe start KProbePass. DriverEntry performs all probes automatically.
Read raw\kernel-probe.txt and confirm CPL=0 and KPROBE COMPLETE; sc.exe query KProbePass must report RUNNING. Stop before each repeat so DriverEntry runs again.
Source uses this pass absolute output path; update it if reproducing in another directory.
controls_and_limitations: Read 64-byte PCI headers via documented HAL API for buses 0..255, no configuration writes. Repeated successfully on both runs.
1234 alone is not uniquely owned by QEMU; the complete 1234:1111 display function and matching revision/class provide the documented identifier.

No MMIO register or BAR validation performed. A deliberately programmed physical device could clone a PCI ID. This is an explicit identifier corroborated by independent privileged interfaces, not a PCI-spec violation.
Headless operation is a lab artifact, but this virtual adapter PCI identity is a separate measured device fact.
